hypotheses.hypothesis: The proposal's lower Gen_bus12 voltage set-point causes the Bus_29 voltage drop from base to proposal.
hypotheses.finding: Against base at the same measurements timestamp, Bus_29 fell from 0.95358 to 0.94212 p.u. (change −0.011464 p.u.); the Gen_bus12 set-point change from 1.025 to 0.950 p.u. accounts for 100% of the change, and undoing it alone restores 0.95358 p.u.

reference.why: the base network at the same moment

result.message: Bus_29 is at 0.942 p.u. at 2000-01-06 18:00 on proposal inj_setpoint, outside its limit (0.950 p.u.); at 2000-01-06 18:00 (the base network at the same moment) it was 0.954 p.u. Of the 0.011 p.u. fall: Voltage set-point of Gen_bus12 (1.025 → 0.950 p.u.) 100 %. Undoing only voltage set-point of Gen_bus12 (1.025 → 0.950 p.u.) would bring Bus_29 back within limits (0.954 p.u.). The main cause depends on the reference: the reference asked for: Voltage set-point of Gen_bus12 (1.025 → 0.950 p.u.); the last moment within limits: Demand near Bus_29 (2 buses); a moment well inside the limits: Demand near Bus_29 (2 buses); the day before: Demand near Bus_29 (2 buses).

assistant:
On proposal **inj_setpoint**, Bus_29 is at **0.942 p.u.** at 18:00 on 6 January, below the **0.950 p.u.** limit; on the base at the same time it is **0.954 p.u.**, within limits.

The cause of the proposal-versus-base drop is the change to **Gen_bus12’s voltage set-point, from 1.025 to 0.950 p.u.** It accounts for the full **0.011 p.u.** decrease in Bus_29 voltage. Undoing just that change restores Bus_29 to **0.954 p.u.** The investigation also found that the main cause can differ when compared against other reference moments, so this finding specifically explains the difference from the base at 18:00.

📋 Data source: measurements
